newsitem.title: LATVIA: RIGA CITY SAYS HAS BBB- S&P CREDIT RATING.
newsitem.headline: RIGA CITY SAYS HAS BBB- S&P CREDIT RATING.

text.p: Latvian capital Riga said on Monday that it has been awarded a BBB- long-term credit rating by Standard & Poor's but was seeking a higher rating.
Riga city finance department deputy director for investment credit questions Inga Cerbule told Reuters that Riga was awarded the rating in January but has not made it public.
She said that the city did not make the rating public as it was not satisfied with it and wanted a higher one.
"Riga council did not distribute this information more widely as we were planning to apply for a new one," Cerbule said.
She said that Riga last week applied for a review of the rating, which it wanted increased to the level of the Latvian state rating, which was BBB.
The city expects the new rating in around one month.
She said that the Latvian capital asked for the rating because it would need investors in the future in the its heating, port and other infrastructure sectors.
She said that a credit rating would be a sign that Riga was a secure investment proposition.
Cerbule said the city wanted the rating even though under finance ministry rules it was not allowed to borrow abroad.
But she noted that even if at the moment the city was not allowed to take loans it was still useful in boosting the city's credibility to have the credit rating.
Latvia in January received a BBB rating by S&P, which put its debt into investment grade class, higher than that of fellow Baltic state, Lithuania.
